name: Multimedia design principles

pinned_evidence.title: Nine Ways to Reduce Cognitive Load in Multimedia Learning
The Cambridge Handbook of Multimedia Learning

evidence.basis: Three decades of controlled experiments on how words and images should be combined. Established principles with the strongest support: multimedia (words plus relevant images beat words alone), coherence (removing interesting-but-extraneous material improves understanding — Mayer, Heiser & Lonn 2001), signalling (cueing the essential improves outcomes — Richter, Scheiter & Eitel meta-analysis), spatial and temporal contiguity (Ginns meta-analysis), and redundancy (duplicating identical content across channels harms rather than helps).
evidence.effect_size_note: Coherence, signalling and contiguity effects replicate across many studies with small-to-moderate effect sizes; the multimedia principle is robust for explanatory content. Animation-versus-static comparisons are mixed and modest, indicating richer media is not automatically better.

mechanism_summary_for_context: How words and images are combined determines whether anything is understood. The findings are specific rather than a general preference for visuals: relevant images alongside words outperform words alone; adding interesting but non-essential material measurably reduces understanding (coherence); cueing what matters improves it (signalling); related words and images must be adjacent in space and time, not separated (contiguity); and presenting the same content twice in two channels degrades rather than reinforces it (redundancy). Notably, richer is not better — animation does not reliably beat static images, and adding immersive richness can increase engagement while reducing comprehension.

preconditions.reason: the principles govern the combination of words and images to explain something; a purely transactional control with no explanatory content has little for them to act on

applicability.culture_note: The processing constraints are general; iconography, reading direction and visual conventions are culturally specific — L3 surface parameters

implementations.generation_directive: Where the content explains how something works, what a product does, or what a result looks like, present it as relevant image or demonstration together with concise words rather than as prose alone. The image must carry the explanatory content, not decorate it — decorative imagery adds load without adding understanding (see coherence).

Remove material that is interesting but not essential to the point being made — tangential detail, decorative media, atmospheric copy. The coherence finding is counterintuitive and specific: adding engaging extras measurably reduces understanding of the core message, even when the extras are enjoyed.

Cue what matters: visual emphasis, hierarchy and structural markers that direct attention to the essential element and the relationship between elements. Signalling improves outcomes without adding content — it tells the reader where capacity should go.

Place words next to the image or control they describe, and present them at the same time — not in separate regions or sequential screens. Conversely, do not present identical content simultaneously in two forms (identical caption duplicating narration, text repeating verbatim what the image already states); duplication competes for the same capacity rather than reinforcing.

hard_rules.rule: Replacing text with imagery may not remove information the user needs to decide — price, terms, limitations and consequences must remain explicit and legible, not implied by a picture
Images used to explain must accurately represent the product or result; illustrative visuals that overstate what the product does are deceptive regardless of medium
Visual-first presentation must retain text alternatives and semantic structure; comprehension gains for some users may not remove access for others

constraints.boundary_test: Does the visual carry the explanation more clearly than words would — or is it decoration that displaced information the user needed?

relations.note: The principles are largely applied cognitive-load management; CL-14 states the capacity constraint, MM-15 specifies word–image handling under it

Picture superiority concerns memory advantage of images over words; MM-15 concerns how the two are combined. Related but distinct claims — PS-13 says images are remembered better, MM-15 says combination rules determine comprehension
Coherent, signalled presentation tends to raise processing fluency; distinct — comprehension versus subjective ease

reference_examples.what: Code and explanation placed side by side at the same moment (contiguity), with signalled structure — explanation adjacent to the thing explained rather than separated
Product demonstrated visually with concise adjacent copy; the image carries the explanation rather than decorating it
Signalled single-focus screens with image and prompt together, sparse of tangential material — coherence and contiguity in a consumer context
